question.problem:
Compute $P(-1<X<0)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12}({x}^{2}+2),\, & -2\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{8} & 1<x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1<X<0) & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{1}{12}({x}^{2}+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+2x]}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}([\frac{1}{3}(0)^{3}+2(0)]-[\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}+2(-1)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(0+\frac{1}{3}+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(\frac{7}{3}) \\  & =\frac{7}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$
